text:
maya: Heads-up: Northern Bank wants a POC with strict EU+UK+Canada residency (no customer data to leave those regions). They also asked for the full sub-processor roster, SCC/DPR language, and an egress cost delta breakdown. Can we triage?
rafael: Do they require dedicated hardware or is pinned hosted acceptable?
megan: They said pinned hosted is preferred for speed of launch, but must support BYOK and explicit no-US-data-plane transfers.
liam: Legal/regulatory note: we can pin data plane to europe-west1 / europe-west2 (UK) / ca-central1. Control-plane orchestration metadata may transit through our control plane region (currently us-east1) unless customer opts into private deployment. We should call that out in Qs.
rafael: Subprocessors that may touch data plane in those regions: GCP (compute + storage), Fastly (edge caching), HashiCorp Vault (optional BYOK). We also use Sentry only for error aggregation (no PII stored in prod logs).
megan: For the sales pitch, what egress multipliers should I quote? customer wants per-token cost delta for pinned CA vs default.
ade: ballpark: ca-central1 +20% per-token, uk (europe-west2) +10%, eu (europe-west1) +12%. Dedicated adds a monthly reserve charge (depends on GPU tier). I'll return with a two-line pricing table.
rafael: Useful snippet to include in the SOW:
```
residency_policy:
  regions: [europe-west1, europe-west2, ca-central1]
  data_plane: pinned
  control_plane: hosted(us-east1)
  kms: BYOK_supported
  egress_adjustments: { ca-central1: 1.20, europe-west2: 1.10, europe-west1: 1.12 }
```
ops-bot: Deployment event: provisioning pinned-dataplane (ca-central1,europe-west1) initiated :package: job=99214
liam: Security questionnaire guidance Q7: "Do you transfer data outside the customer region?" Suggested answer: "Data plane is pinned to the customer-selected region(s). Control-plane orchestration metadata may traverse other regions; we offer Private deployments for zero-control-plane egress. See attached attestation and SCC annex."
megan: They specifically asked about EU->US transfers and adequacy. We should indicate SCCs and DPF compliance where applicable and whether any subprocessors invoke US transfers.
rafael: Current state: no automatic data-plane transfer to US. Subprocessor transfers: Vault (if used) may have a US control plane option but can be configured in-region; Fastly caching edge nodes may touch headers but we can request no-logs config.
maya: Customer asked if we can run a 1% EU+UK canary for 48 hours to measure latency & token throughput before full cutover. Any blockers?
ade: Canary is ok on hosted pinned, but SLOs for latency under bursty traffic are not guaranteed unless they move to Reserved/Dedicated. Pricing for a 48hr canary: negligible extra besides egress multiplier; dedicated requires a monthly reservation. I'll put numbers in deal room.
megan: Can ops/infra provide a short attestation list (subproc, country, transfer direction, cert link)? Need to include exact URLs in the security response.
liam: I'll upload the attestation + SCC annex link to the shared folder by EOD and confirm which subprocessors rely on EU-US DPF/SCC.
maya: Great. I'll bundle the answers into the SOW template and update the customer. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
